q: An optical instrument used for viewing ____ objects is called a telescope.
e: Telescopes are specifically designed to magnify distant objects.

q: The refracting astronomical telescope consists of an objective of long focal length and an eyepiece of ____ focal length.
e: A short focal length eyepiece provides higher magnification.

q: Both lenses in a refracting astronomical telescope are ____ lenses.
e: Refracting telescopes use convex lenses to gather and focus light.
Galileo Galilei famously developed and used the refracting telescope for astronomy.

q: A real and inverted image of a distant object is formed at the ____ of the objective.
e: Distant objects form their real image precisely at the focal point of the objective lens.

q: The final image formed by the eyepiece of an astronomical telescope is virtual, larger than the first image and ____ with respect to the distant object.
e: Astronomical telescopes produce an inverted final image, which is acceptable for viewing stars.

q: The magnifying power of the refracting astronomical telescope is defined as the ratio of the angle subtended by the ____ seen by the eye to the angle subtended by the object.
e: Magnifying power compares the angular size of the image to the angular size of the object.

q: To obtain the sharp images of distant objects the objective should have a large ____.
e: A larger objective diameter gathers more light and improves resolving power.

q: In practice, a ____ mirror instead of a convex lens is used as an objective in reflecting telescopes.
e: Large concave mirrors avoid the chromatic aberration and weight issues of large lenses.

q: The reflecting telescope was first suggested by Newton and this arrangement is called the ____ design.
e: The Newtonian design uses a secondary flat mirror to direct light to an eyepiece on the side.

q: It is not convenient to use the astronomical telescope for viewing objects on the earth since the final image produced is ____.
e: Terrestrial viewing requires an erect image, unlike astronomical viewing.

q: In the terrestrial telescope a ____ lens is used as an eyepiece to produce a final image which is erect.
e: A concave eyepiece (Galilean design) produces an erect image without needing extra erecting lenses.

q: Total reflecting prisms are used in ____ to reduce the length of the terrestrial telescope.
e: Binoculars use Porro or roof prisms to fold the optical path, making them compact.

q: Because of the successive total internal ____ in the prisms, the length of the telescope is greatly reduced.
e: Total internal reflection inside prisms folds the light path, shortening the physical tube.
